newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine Weather-Dry spell seen delaying harvest.
newsitem.headline: Philippine Weather-Dry spell seen delaying harvest.

text.p: Some Philippine rice lands have received below normal rainfall in recent weeks despite the country having entered the peak months of its rainy season, agriculture and weather experts said on Tuesday.
"We are having enough rains except for the northern Ilocos region," said Bureau of Soils and and Water Management director Rogelio Concepcion.
Concepcion did not say how much of the country's rice harvests comes from the Ilocos region.
"It's been raining in most parts of the country since the start of the week because we are at the peak of our rainy season," said Ernesto Verceles at the Philippine weather bureau.
"However, rains in western Luzon island is less than 50 percent than the normal volume (in recent days)," he added.
The rainy season starts in April and lasts up to September.
Concepcion said he expected the full impact of the drop in the volume of rainfall to be felt in the country in the fourth quarter.
"For now, farmers are happy because we have not experienced destructive typhoons. This is favourable to crops because of alternate days of rains and sunlight," he said.
"However, this is not a reason for us to drop our guard because of forecasts by our weather experts of a drought starting in the fourth quarter," Concepcion added.
Concepcion's department plans to conduct cloud seeding over four major dams in the country to induce rain starting in October to mitigate the impact of a drought caused by the El Nino phenomenon.
El Nino is caused by the warming of water in the western Pacific ocean, which interacts with other weather such as drought in some areas and heavier-than-normal rainfall in others.
Concepcion said he expected a delay in rice planting in the fourth quarter because of prospects of a drought. "This would lead to a drop in harvests in the first quarter of the year."

In an El Nino advisory early this month, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa) said major portions of the country received below normal rainfalls between April and June this year.
It said the volume of rains brought by three cyclones that hit the Philippines in the same period were also lower than expected.
The weather bureau said it expected the rains in most parts of the country between July and September this year to be below normal volumes due to El Nino.
